text:
kai: Heads-up — noticed a weird P95 regression after we enabled the new continuous-batching smoothing. Latency spikes coincide with KV-cache churn and a bunch of small requests.

maria: ugh. any flamegraphs or traces? :eyes:

kai: yeah attaching quick trace summary — the worker queues are getting tiny batches interleaved with big ones. here's the admit config we rolled out:

```yaml
admit:
  policy: leaky_bucket
  rate_per_sec: 320
  burst_tokens: 800
  token_budget_target: 0.06   # target fraction of tokens per request used to form batches
  soft_reject_pct: 0.10      # allow soft 10% soft-429s
  smoothing_window_ms: 50
```

liam: interesting. token_budget_target 0.06 seems aggressive for tail-heavy workloads. KV-cache misses will force longer model time, which reduces our effective batching opportunities and sidelines the leaky bucket refill assumptions.

tanvi: can you show hit-rate vs batch-size correlation? my hypothesis: when KV hit drops < 0.7 batch-size collapses and we start emitting soft rejects which amplify the problem.

kai: copied from perf dashboard (synth):
- KV hit: 0.82 -> 0.66 during regen
- avg batch size: 8.3 -> 3.1
- P95 latency: 160ms -> 330ms
- soft-429 rate: 0.12 -> 0.27

maria: that soft-429 feedback loop is classic. clients retry and create more small requests -> more misses -> more soft rejects. We should break the loop with one of: (a) raise token_budget_target, (b) temporarily prioritize KV-warmup, or (c) clamp soft_reject_pct and prefer queueing with degraded latency.

liam: +1 to (a) as first pass. If we increase token_budget_target from 0.06 -> 0.12 we let the admit logic wait a bit longer to accumulate tokens. But need guardrails to avoid head-of-line latency for very large requests.

tanvi: we can add per-request max-wait-ms: 120 so we don't hold very long. Also consider a dynamic short-term KV-warmup: if KV hit drops > 10% in last 30s, raise burst_tokens by 2x for 60s to let cached prefixes form.

kai: trying tweak locally: increased token_budget_target to 0.12 and set max_wait_ms=120. Quick canary on a single ring shows batch size back to ~7 and P95 back to 180ms. soft-429 down to 0.05.

maria: love that. what's the rollout plan? this feels safe but still impacts tail for large requests.

liam: plan: canary 5% 1h -> observe P50/P95, retry amplification, and error budget use. If stable, 25% 3h -> full. Also add a monitoring alert for "admit:soft_reject_rate > 0.08 for 10m".

tanvi: also add a profiler job to capture kernel selection distribution around canary windows. I suspect certain long-seq paths trigger different kernel choices and exacerbate batching mismatch.

kai: noted. profiler query (prom):
```
sum by(kernel) (rate(kernel_execution_count[1m]))
/ sum(rate(kernel_execution_count[1m]))
```

maria: aside: consider changing soft_reject behavior to return header X-Soft-Reject: true so clients can do backoff jitter instead of immediate retry.

liam: good call. that reduces thundering herd. also add opt-in header for clients to accept 202+poll instead of 429.

ops-bot: deploy started: admit-config update -> canary ring (5%) by rollout-job #admit-238. CI checks passed.

kai: after 20m in canary: KV hit normalized to 0.79, avg batch 6.9, P95 175ms. No retry storms yet.

maria: sounds good. let's keep canary for 2h and then follow the 25% step. create a short runbook note for SRE on how to revert: set token_budget_target back to 0.06 and reduce burst_tokens to 800.

tanvi: I'll add the kernel-sampling profiler and a dashboard panel for KvHit vs BatchSize and a derived metric: effective_token_rate = tokens_processed / active_workers.

liam: one more thought — add a small hysteresis to soft_reject_pct so it ramps down only if batch_size sustained > 6 for 5m. avoids flip-flop.

kai: added to config for next iteration. thanks all. cc @maria for runbook and @liam for alerts.

maria: on it. will post runbook snippet here when done. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: canary reached 5% (stable for 30m).
